producer_observations: 17 classes, 9 enums, 17 slots; imports linkml:types, malleus, metrology, chronology, research; history profile source-assertion
seven classes extend a Malleus root directly and each carries its own grounding block: GeologicFeature, GeologicMaterial, SeismicEvent, DigitalResource, ResearchAgent, GeologicRelation, AgentRelation

ten classes derive through a pack or project type and carry none: Melt, Dataset, SoftwarePackage, NumericalModel, ReportedClaim, DepthObservation, CountObservation, ReportedRatio, BibliographicSource, FundingRelation

every number is an Observation whose subject is the named thing, not a slot on that thing, because the reading states approximate values, open bounds, ranges, measured values and modelled values and value_qualification, unit, uncertainty and determination have to travel with each one

two Observation subclasses only: DepthObservation adds depth_reference because the reading states depths below the sea floor and depths below sea level, and CountObservation keeps a count an integer with its scope; the proxy an estimate rests on is an OBSERVED_WITH relation to a Method and not a new slot

the Event family is narrow: only occurrents the source identifies individually. Earthquake populations are Observations whose subject is the place they lie beneath, which also keeps them reachable, since relation endpoints and subject are Entity-ranged and cannot point at an Event
bearings stay as written (orientation_as_stated); reading a compass bearing as a number is a normalization needing its own evidence

the producer's self-check is a shape pass over one file (block placement, the three closed grounding forms, compiler-bindable ranges, no name collisions with the closure), four PASS; it names the slot_usage narrowing of agent_type on ResearchAgent as the likeliest refusal site. The gate accepted the file at attempt 01 and no diagnostic was returned.

citation_check.by: the cell's agent, after ONTOLOGY_READY and before phase two
citation_check.method: the ontology's grounding blocks parsed with yaml, then every distinct vocabulary_url fetched and every borrowed term looked for in what came back
citation_check.checked_at_source: the harness transcript's timestamps of the WebFetch calls
citation_check.urls_note: Four distinct URLs over six vocabulary blocks: GeoSPARQL is cited twice (GeologicFeature and GeologicRelation) and PROV-O twice (ResearchAgent and AgentRelation).
citation_check.result: opengis.net/ont/geosparql# redirects (303) to defs.opengis.net/prez-backend/object?uri=https://www.opengis.net/ont/geosparql, which declares all five borrowed terms: Feature, SpatialObject, sfWithin, sfContains, sfTouches. w3.org/TR/prov-o/ declares all five: Agent, Person, Organization, actedOnBehalfOf, wasAttributedTo. dublincore.org/specifications/dublin-core/dcmi-terms/ declares all three: Dataset and Software in the DCMI Type Vocabulary and identifier as a property. quakeml.org does not serve over TLS under that name (the certificate is for quake.ethz.ch); the vocabulary's current home quake.ethz.ch/quakeml/ was fetched instead, and its landing page, its BasicEventDescription and BasicEventDescriptionTypes pages carry the QuakeML 2.0 package structure with the type declarations only inside linked UML PDFs. The RFC index at quake.ethz.ch/quakeml/RFC_BED_1.0 names 'Event, Origin' and 'Magnitude' as Basic Event Description elements under discussion but declares none of them. Event, Origin and Magnitude are therefore recorded as unverified, not as fabricated: the vocabulary is real, the terms are named as its elements on its own site, and no page fetched carries the declaration.
citation_check.none_found_block: GeologicMaterial takes the none_found form outright, with the search recorded and four terms declared invented. The producer's stated reason: the declared inputs carry no material vocabulary and the session has no network, so nothing could be vouched for. That is the honest form and not a defect.
